Procurements—Notice and Represen tation (OCT 2025) (a) Definitions. As used in this provision— Foreign person means any person other than a United States person. Specified Federal procurement payment means any payment made pursuant to a contract with a foreign contracting party that is for goods, manufactured or produced, or services provided in a foreign country that is not a party to an international procurement agreement with the United States. For purposes of the prior sentence, a foreign country does not include an outlying area of the United States. United States person as defined in 26 U.S.C. 7701(a)(30) means (1) A citizen or resident of the United States; (2) A domestic partnership; (3) A domestic corporation; (4) Any estate (other than a foreign estate, within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. 701(a)(31)); and (5) Any trust if– (i) A court within the United States is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of the trust; and (ii) One or more United States persons have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust. (b) Unless exempted, there is a 2 percent tax of the amount of a specified Federal procurement payment on any foreign person receiving such payment. See 26 U.S.C. 5000C and its implementing regulations at 26 CFR 1.5000C- 1

rmed as per the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 25, Standard for Inspections, Testing, and Maintenance of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems and all other associated NFPA Standards. This is considered a remote location, and connectivity can be an issue. Background YOSE has over 138 fire suppression systems in buildings parkwide. Each system is inspected each year and deficiencies identified. This project is to bring the fire suppression systems in the El Portal Residences known as the Motor Inn Cabins, Yosemite Valley residences, Wawona District residences, and Mather District residences into compliance with NFPA requirements. This project encompasses a total of 40 locations and represents 43 individual fire suppression systems. The contractor will perform tasks to rectify the fire suppression system deficiencies identified during the annual inspections. Deficiencies include the following, but not limited to interval testing, replace missing signage, replacing air and water gauges, installing electric bells, replacing recalled sprinkler heads, adding wrenches and heads for head boxes, replacing painted sprinkler heads, adjustment of water flow switches, and performing system inspections with passing reports.
